models_evaluated: 10 AI chatbots (3 multimodal, 7 unimodal; anonymized as chatbots 1-10)

links.outcome: Chatbot accuracy on oncology case questions, multiple-choice versus free-text
links.effect: Top multiple-choice accuracy was 72.15% (57/79), while top free-text accuracy was only 37.97% (30/79). Nine of 10 chatbots, including all 3 multimodal chatbots, had lower free-text than multiple-choice accuracy.
links.quote: Nine out of 10 chatbots, including all 3 multimodal chatbots, demonstrated decreased accuracy of their free-text responses compared with multiple-choice responses to questions about cancer cases.

links.outcome: Multimodal chatbot accuracy on cases with multiple images versus single images
links.effect: Accuracy of multimodal chatbots decreased on cases with multiple images compared with questions with single images.
links.quote: The accuracy of multimodal chatbots decreased when tested on cases with multiple images compared with questions with single images.

unlisted_practices: zero-shot chain-of-thought prompt engineering to improve chatbot accuracy

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates multimodal and unimodal AI chatbots on clinical oncology cases and specifically tests the utility of a prompting technique (zero-shot chain-of-thought).
